title: DevOps
tagline: Beginner-friendly DevOps training and internship — from Linux and Git to CI/CD, Kubernetes, and AWS deployment.
description: A beginner-friendly DevOps Basics Training & Internship Program. Month 1 is structured training: three self-paced recorded classes and one live doubt-clarification session every week, plus a hands-on task tied to that week's topic. Month 2 is a project phase — applying everything you learned to take a real app from Git through Docker, a CI/CD pipeline, and deployment on AWS, with weekly live mentoring.
outcomes: Administer Linux systems and manage code with Git & GitHub
Containerize applications with Docker and Docker Compose
Build CI/CD pipelines with Jenkins and GitHub Actions
Deploy a containerized application to AWS EC2, with foundational Kubernetes knowledge
Take a project end-to-end: Git → Docker → CI/CD → AWS deployment

topics: Class 1: Linux basics — file system, users, permissions, basic commands
Class 2: Shell scripting basics + package management
Class 3: Git & GitHub — repos, commits, branches, pull requests
Live session: doubt clarification on Linux commands & Git workflow
Task: set up a GitHub repo and practice basic Linux and Git commands
Class 1: Docker introduction — images vs containers, installing Docker
Class 2: Writing a Dockerfile, building images
Class 3: Docker Compose basics — running multi-container apps
Live session: doubt clarification on Docker
Task: containerize a simple sample application using Docker
Class 1: CI/CD concepts — build, test, deploy stages
Class 2: Jenkins basics — installing Jenkins, creating a simple pipeline
Class 3: GitHub Actions basics — writing a workflow YAML file
Live session: doubt clarification on pipeline setup
Task: create a basic CI/CD pipeline (Jenkins or GitHub Actions) for the Dockerized app
Class 1: Kubernetes basics — pods, deployments, services (conceptual + light hands-on)
Class 2: AWS basics — EC2, S3, IAM overview
Class 3: Deploying the containerized app to an AWS EC2 instance
Live session: doubt clarification + wrap-up of Month 1 topics
Task: deploy the sample app to AWS and document the deployment steps
Apply Weeks 1–4 together: take the app from Git → Docker → CI/CD pipeline → AWS deployment
Weekly live mentoring session for project progress and doubts
Final week: project demo plus basic documentation (README + steps followed)

projects: End-to-end capstone: take a sample app from Git through Docker, a CI/CD pipeline, and deployment on AWS EC2
Weekly hands-on tasks: GitHub repo setup, a Dockerized app, a CI/CD pipeline, and an AWS EC2 deployment

faqs.a: Yes — this program is designed for complete beginners, starting from Linux and Git fundamentals with no prior DevOps experience required.
12 self-paced recorded lecture classes, 4 live doubt-clarification sessions in Month 1, weekly live mentoring in Month 2, one end-to-end deployed project, and a certificate of completion.

faqs.q: Will I get hands-on cloud practice?
faqs.a: Yes — the Month 2 project phase has you deploy a real containerized app to AWS EC2, not a simulation.

faqs.q: What's the difference between Live and Self-Paced?
faqs.a: Live batches include instructor-led sessions, real-time doubt clearing, and mentorship. Self-Paced gives you the recorded content on your own schedule. Both include the same projects and certificate.
